name: bk-vo-1
text:
The tallest building on Earth... stands on sand. [short pause] Eight hundred and twenty-eight metres. And no solid bedrock to grab.

Dig under Burj Khalifa and you hit loose sand, then about seventy metres of weak, crumbly sandstone. Salty water sits just two and a half metres down.

So the engineers stopped looking for rock. [pause] They used grip.

One hundred and ninety-two concrete piles. Each one and a half metres wide... driven about fifty metres down. They hold mostly by friction. Like pushing your hand deep into a sack of rice.

On top, a concrete raft three point seven metres thick.

And the salt? An electric current runs under it, protecting the steel.

So is it standing on sand... or gripping it?
